content: Abacavir sulfate, marketed under the brand name Ziagen, is a synthetic carbocyclic nucleoside analogue with inhibitory activity against HIV-1. Its chemical name is (1S, cis)-4-[2-amino-6-(cyclopropylamino)-9H-purin-9-yl]-2-cyclopentene-1-methanol sulfate (salt) (2:1). The compound exists as the enantiomer with an absolute configuration of 1S, 4R on the cyclopentene ring. Abacavir sulfate appears as a white to off-white solid and has a solubility of approximately 77 mg/mL in distilled water at 25°C. Ziagen is available in tablet form for oral administration, with each tablet containing abacavir sulfate equivalent to 300 mg of abacavir as the active ingredient. The tablets also include the following inactive ingredients: colloidal silicon dioxide, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, and sodium starch glycolate. The tablets are coated with a film composed of hypromellose, polysorbate 80, synthetic yellow iron oxide, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. Ziagen is also available as an oral solution for oral administration, containing 20 mg/mL of abacavir as the active ingredient. The oral solution includes the following inactive ingredients: artificial strawberry and banana flavors, anhydrous citric acid, methylparaben and propylparaben (used as preservatives), propylene glycol, saccharin sodium, sodium citrate dihydrate, sorbitol solution, and water. In vivo, abacavir sulfate dissociates into its free base, abacavir. All dosages of Ziagen are expressed in terms of the abacavir content.
